founder_decisions.text: Care Operations owns execution and documentation of routine, nonclinical horse-care work, including turnout, stall care, water checks, blanketing, fly protection, grooming, hoof picking, routine body and environmental observations, authorized hand walking, housing coordination, care rounds, exceptions, and permitted owner summaries. It does not own diagnosis, veterinary instructions, medication truth, nutrition formulation, billing liability, employment discipline, or ownership.

Care Operations may display and execute authorized feed, supplement, medication, and treatment instructions, but the substantive instruction and authoritative record remain with the applicable Feed/Nutrition or Health/Medication domain.
A care plan is a governed, versioned operational record. Free-text notes may supplement but may not silently override structured instructions.

Care instructions may exist at horse, facility default, location or group, temporary stay or event, and seasonal or condition-based levels. Authorized horse-specific instructions take precedence with visible conflict handling.

Only actors with explicit role, relationship, horse, facility, and purpose authority may create or change care instructions. Assignment to perform care does not grant authority to alter the instruction.

Staff may make bounded safe operational substitutions but may not materially change care, diet, medication, housing restrictions, turnout compatibility, protective equipment, or professional instructions without authority. Emergency protective action must be recorded and escalated.

Assignments may target a named person, qualified role or team, open authorized queue, temporary substitute, supervised assignee, or recurring shift. Responsibility and actual performer must remain attributable.
Completion requires affirmative attestation. Higher-risk work may require structured fields, reason codes, measurements, second checks, or evidence. Time passage never auto-completes care.
Care workers may record observable facts but not diagnosis or professional conclusions.
Escalation uses four standardized semantic levels: Routine Note, Attention Required, Urgent, and Emergency. Timing targets may be configurable.
EquineSync may guide and document emergency escalation but does not replace human judgment, professionals, emergency services, or facility plans. Delivery must not be represented as receipt.
Overdue or missed care remains open until completed, excused, superseded, authorized-cancelled, documented impossible, or escalated and resolved. No silent auto-completion.

Care Operations owns the current operational location and housing assignment used for care coordination, while Horse Lifecycle and Facility domains own horse and facility identity. Moves preserve prior and new location, effective time, reason, authority, performer, and temporary status.
The system may display compatibility facts, warnings, restrictions, and templates, but may not autonomously determine that horses are safe together. Suggestions remain advisory and human-approved.
Condition-based care may use weather and environmental inputs. Warnings and proposed tasks are allowed, but high-risk care decisions may not be autonomously executed without later narrow approval.
Blanketing, fly protection, boots, masks, wraps, and similar routine equipment may use structured instructions. Routine protective equipment must remain distinct from medical or treatment equipment.

Authorized owners and guardians may see permitted care status, material exceptions, relevant observations, and selected evidence, but not internal staffing commentary, unrelated records, restricted investigations, protected safeguarding information, or other horses' data.

Photo, video, measurement, scan, or signature evidence is configurable rather than universally required. Designated high-risk or disputed activities may require evidence with preserved metadata, authorship, time, horse association, permissions, retention, and correction.

Initial scope must support low-connectivity care work with bounded cached instructions, completion and exception capture, observations, evidence, queued timestamps, visible unsynchronized status, and deterministic reconciliation without broadening offline access.

AI is limited to bounded assistance such as drafting summaries, routing observations, identifying duplicates or missing records, and transcription. AI may not diagnose, alter care, prescribe treatment, decide compatibility, close tasks, suppress escalation, make emergency decisions, or present welfare conclusions as fact.

requirements.statement: The system SHALL treat routine nonclinical care execution and documentation as the primary Care Operations scope.

The system SHALL prevent Care Operations from becoming the authoritative source for diagnosis, veterinary instructions, medication truth, nutrition formulation, billing liability, employment discipline, or horse ownership.
The system SHALL preserve one authoritative owner for each care instruction, record, state, and decision.
The system SHALL display authoritative external feed, medication, treatment, or professional instructions without permitting Care Operations to silently mutate their substantive meaning.
The system SHALL record execution facts separately from substantive instruction truth.
The system SHALL represent care plans as versioned governed records with effective dates, applicability, source, authority, and supersession.
The system SHALL prevent unstructured notes from silently overriding structured active instructions.
The system SHALL resolve instruction applicability across horse, facility, location or group, temporary stay, event, season, and condition levels.
The system SHALL visibly surface conflicts among applicable instructions and require authorized resolution or a fail-safe treatment.
The system SHALL authorize care-plan creation and modification by actor, relationship, horse, facility, purpose, delegation, and time.
The system SHALL not infer instruction-edit authority from assignment to perform a task.
The system SHALL support bounded safe substitutions while preserving the original instruction, substitution reason, performer, time, and escalation where required.
The system SHALL require immediate recording and escalation of emergency protective actions taken outside the ordinary instruction.
The system SHALL support assignment to a named person, qualified role or team, authorized open queue, temporary substitute, supervised assignee, and recurring shift.
The system SHALL preserve both accountable responsibility and actual performer for every completed, missed, substituted, or cancelled care task.
The system SHALL require affirmative completion attestation by an authenticated or otherwise authorized attributable performer.
The system SHALL support configurable evidence, structured fields, reason codes, measurements, and second checks for designated task types.
The system SHALL never auto-complete a care task solely because its due time passed.
The system SHALL support start, pause, resume, block, complete, exception, miss, excuse, supersede, cancel, and correct states where applicable.
The system SHALL maintain an unresolved-care queue across shifts and handoffs.
The system SHALL record task completion with horse, instruction version, location, performer, responsible assignee, timestamps, result, evidence, offline status, and sync status.
The system SHALL prevent duplicate completion from retries or repeated synchronization through idempotency and authoritative reconciliation.
The system SHALL permit factual observations while labeling them as observations rather than diagnoses or professional conclusions.
The system SHALL preserve observation wording, structured values, source, author, time, horse, location, attachments, and later correction history.
The system SHALL provide four standardized escalation meanings: Routine Note, Attention Required, Urgent, and Emergency.
The system SHALL allow configurable response targets without changing the semantic meaning of escalation levels.
The system SHALL record escalation recipients, delivery attempts, delivery status, acknowledgments, actions, and closure evidence.
The system SHALL distinguish notification sent, delivered, opened, acknowledged, and acted upon.
The system SHALL provide prominent human contact actions and applicable authorized emergency context without representing software as a professional or emergency service.
The system SHALL preserve critical authorized emergency information for bounded offline access where policy permits.
The system SHALL keep overdue or missed care open until an authorized terminal treatment is recorded.
The system SHALL require reasons and authority for excusal, cancellation, supersession, impossibility, or exception closure.
The system SHALL expose recurring misses and unresolved exceptions without reducing care quality to completion percentage alone.
The system SHALL maintain current operational horse location and housing assignment for care coordination while referencing canonical horse and facility identities.
The system SHALL preserve prior location, new location, effective time, reason, authorizing actor, executing actor, and temporary or continuing status for movement.
The system SHALL prevent a task or care workflow from rewriting canonical facility hierarchy or permanent horse identity.
The system SHALL display turnout compatibility facts, restrictions, warnings, and approved group templates without autonomously declaring a pairing safe.
The system SHALL require authorized human approval for any advisory turnout grouping suggestion.
The system SHALL support weather and environmental condition inputs with freshness, source, location, and uncertainty indicators.
The system SHALL permit warnings and proposed tasks from environmental rules while prohibiting autonomous high-risk care decisions unless separately approved.
The system SHALL support structured protective-equipment instructions, including item or type, fit or placement, use conditions, inspections, removal, damage handling, and responsibility.
The system SHALL distinguish routine protective equipment from medical devices or treatment equipment.
The system SHALL provide owner and guardian projections limited to permitted care status, material exceptions, relevant observations, and selected evidence.

The system SHALL exclude internal staffing commentary, unrelated employee or customer data, other horses, protected investigations, and restricted safeguarding material from ordinary owner projections.
The system SHALL prevent facility visibility configuration from suppressing material welfare exceptions that policy requires to be disclosed.
The system SHALL preserve media evidence metadata, authorship, capture and upload time, horse association, access policy, retention class, and correction or withdrawal history.
The system SHALL make evidence requirements configurable by task type, condition, dispute state, and release class.
The system SHALL support bounded offline viewing of recently synchronized assigned care and critical authorized instructions.
The system SHALL support offline capture of completion, exceptions, observations, and evidence with clear pending status.
The system SHALL revalidate authorization, instruction version, horse state, location, and conflicts when offline operations synchronize.
The system SHALL encrypt offline data and enforce device, account, tenant, horse, purpose, and expiry boundaries.
The system SHALL provide deterministic accepted, rejected, conflicted, or quarantined outcomes for synchronized operations.
The system SHALL label AI-assisted content and preserve source and reviewer attribution.
The system SHALL require human review before AI-assisted text becomes an owner-visible summary or authoritative care record.
The system SHALL prohibit AI from diagnosing, prescribing, changing instructions, deciding compatibility, closing work, suppressing escalation, or making emergency decisions.
The system SHALL provide an accessible correction and contest path for AI-assisted output.

The system SHALL preserve attributable audit events for care-plan changes, assignments, completion, exceptions, observations, escalation, evidence, corrections, owner projections, exports, and administrative action.
The system SHALL provide administrative tools for authorized correction, reassignment, conflict review, sync quarantine, evidence restriction, escalation review, and account or device revocation.

The system SHALL expose operational metrics and alerts for unresolved urgent work, failed emergency delivery, stale instructions, sync backlog, duplicate attempts, authorization denial anomalies, and evidence-processing failures.
The system SHALL define backup, restore, rollback, incident, support, and maintenance procedures before production or first-user enrollment.
The system SHALL preserve historical truth through correction and supersession rather than silent overwrite or destructive deletion.
The system SHALL support purpose-limited search, reports, and exports without creating employee surveillance or unsupported welfare conclusions.
The system SHALL meet approved accessibility, mobile, low-connectivity, performance, security, privacy, and data-integrity baselines.
The system SHALL not claim implementation, operational readiness, or enrollment readiness without the applicable evidence and Founder disposition.

workflows.name: Create or amend care plan
workflows.summary: Authorized care authority proposes, validates, reviews conflicts, records source and applicability, obtains required approval, activates a version, and preserves the prior version.

workflows.name: Generate daily care queue
workflows.summary: The system resolves active instructions, schedule rules, horse state, location, assignments, and exceptions into a permission-filtered shift queue.

workflows.name: Assign, claim, substitute, or reassign care
workflows.summary: An authorized actor assigns responsibility or an eligible worker claims work; substitutions preserve accountability, qualification, and reason.

workflows.name: Perform and attest routine care
workflows.summary: The performer verifies horse and instruction, records result, evidence and exception, attests completion, and receives an authoritative status.

workflows.name: Record welfare observation
workflows.summary: The worker records factual observations, selects severity, attaches evidence if allowed, and routes for review without diagnosis.

workflows.name: Urgent or emergency escalation
workflows.summary: The user triggers the appropriate level, contacts humans directly, records delivery and acknowledgment, and preserves chronology until resolved.

workflows.name: Handle overdue, missed, blocked, or impossible care
workflows.summary: The task remains open, reason and authority are recorded, escalation and handoff occur, and closure uses an authorized terminal treatment.

workflows.name: Move horse or change housing assignment
workflows.summary: Authorized actor validates destination and restrictions, records effective move, updates operational location, and preserves movement history.

workflows.name: Apply weather-responsive care rule
workflows.summary: Fresh environmental data produces a warning or proposed task; an authorized person confirms high-risk action and records the decision.

workflows.name: Apply, inspect, change, or remove protective equipment
workflows.summary: The worker verifies the item and instruction, records fit or damage, completes or escalates, and preserves evidence when required.

workflows.name: Work offline and synchronize
workflows.summary: Authorized data is cached, actions are captured as pending, synchronization revalidates authority and versions, and conflicts are accepted, rejected, or quarantined.

workflows.name: Publish owner care summary
workflows.summary: Permitted source facts are projected, AI assistance is reviewed if used, sensitive material is excluded, and publication is attributable.

workflows.name: Correct or supersede care record
workflows.summary: Authorized correction preserves original values, reason, evidence, affected downstream records, notices, and successor linkage.

workflows.name: Shift handoff and continuity
workflows.summary: Outgoing and incoming workers review unresolved work, urgent observations, horse locations, changed instructions, and sync conflicts with acknowledgment.

entities.name: HorseOperationalLocation

entities.name: HorseMovementRecord

entities.name: TurnoutConstraintReference
entities.purpose: Referenced compatibility facts, restrictions, warnings, and approved group template.

entities.name: ProtectiveEquipmentInstruction

entities.name: EnvironmentalConditionSnapshot

entities.name: CareHandoff

entities.name: OfflineCareOperation

entities.name: OwnerCareProjection

entities.name: CareConfiguration

entities.name: CareAuditReference

state_models.states: DRAFT -> PENDING_APPROVAL -> ACTIVE -> SUSPENDED or SUPERSEDED or EXPIRED -> ARCHIVED
state_models.rule: Only an authorized plan authority may activate, suspend, supersede, or archive.

state_models.states: SCHEDULED -> AVAILABLE -> CLAIMED -> IN_PROGRESS -> COMPLETED, EXCEPTION, MISSED, CANCELLED, or SUPERSEDED
state_models.rule: No time-based auto-completion; correction preserves original completion.

state_models.states: DRAFT -> SUBMITTED -> TRIAGED -> ESCALATED or ACKNOWLEDGED -> RESOLVED -> ARCHIVED; CORRECTED may supersede
OPEN -> ROUTING -> NOTIFIED -> ACKNOWLEDGED -> ACTIONING -> RESOLVED -> CLOSED; DELIVERY_FAILED remains visible
state_models.rule: Sent does not equal received or acknowledged.

state_models.states: PROPOSED -> ACTIVE -> ENDING -> ENDED; CORRECTED or DISPUTED are preserved branches
state_models.rule: Canonical horse and facility identities are referenced, not rewritten.

state_models.states: LOCAL_PENDING -> QUEUED -> SYNCING -> ACCEPTED, REJECTED, CONFLICTED, or QUARANTINED
DRAFT -> REVIEWED -> PUBLISHED -> CORRECTED, WITHDRAWN, or SUPERSEDED
state_models.rule: Restricted source content never becomes visible through projection.

permission_rules.boundary: Cannot diagnose, alter professional instructions, or view unrelated tenants

permission_rules.allowed: Create or approve care plans within authority, assign work, resolve routine exceptions, initiate escalations
permission_rules.boundary: Cannot broaden access or override health, medication, safeguarding, or ownership authority

permission_rules.allowed: Create or amend authorized horse-specific routine care instructions and view assigned horses
permission_rules.boundary: No authority from trainer label alone; no unrelated facility or horse access

permission_rules.allowed: View minimum assigned instructions, perform care, record facts and exceptions, escalate
permission_rules.boundary: Cannot edit underlying instructions unless separately authorized

permission_rules.allowed: View permitted owner projection, propose or approve instructions where relationship grants authority, contest records
permission_rules.boundary: Cannot view internal personnel data, other horses, or restricted investigations

permission_rules.allowed: View and act only within the protected participant and horse authority granted
permission_rules.boundary: No authority inferred from payment or relationship label alone

permission_rules.allowed: View explicitly shared horse context and create professional records in provider domain
permission_rules.boundary: Cannot receive broad care-operations access or mutate non-provider care plans without grant

permission_rules.allowed: Case-bound troubleshooting, metadata and sync review, controlled correction assistance
permission_rules.boundary: No silent care decision, diagnosis, instruction change, or unrestricted content access

permission_rules.allowed: Generate tasks, route notices, reconcile sync, calculate due state under approved rules
permission_rules.boundary: Cannot create product policy, auto-complete care, or infer authority

permission_rules.boundary: Cannot diagnose, prescribe, decide compatibility, close work, suppress escalation, or create authority

api_contracts.name: Resolve applicable care instructions
api_contracts.behavior: Returns permission-filtered active instruction set with source, version, precedence, conflicts, and freshness.

api_contracts.name: Create or amend care plan proposal
api_contracts.behavior: Accepts authorized proposal and expected version; returns draft or conflict.

api_contracts.name: Activate care plan version
api_contracts.behavior: Requires authority and approvals; emits activation and supersession events.

api_contracts.name: Create or materialize care task
api_contracts.behavior: Uses approved task type, instruction, schedule, horse, location, and idempotency key.

api_contracts.name: Assign, claim, substitute, or reassign
api_contracts.behavior: Validates qualification and authority; preserves responsibility lineage.

api_contracts.name: Attest task result
api_contracts.behavior: Records completion or exception with expected version and evidence references.

api_contracts.name: Submit observation
api_contracts.behavior: Creates factual observation and optional escalation request.

api_contracts.name: Open or update escalation
api_contracts.behavior: Routes notices and records delivery, acknowledgment, and action chronology.

api_contracts.name: Change operational location
api_contracts.behavior: Validates horse, facility location, restrictions, authority, and effective time.

api_contracts.name: Submit offline operation batch
api_contracts.behavior: Processes idempotent operations with per-item accepted, rejected, conflicted, or quarantined result.

api_contracts.name: Create owner care projection
api_contracts.behavior: Builds minimum-necessary projection and requires review where configured.

api_contracts.name: Correct or supersede record
api_contracts.behavior: Creates successor with reason, authority, downstream impact, and audit linkage.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: An unauthorized worker cannot create, activate, or change a care instruction.
A worker assigned to perform care can view only the minimum horse, instruction, location, and evidence context required.
Changing an active care plan creates a new version and preserves the prior version and effective interval.
A free-text note cannot override an active structured instruction.
Conflicting applicable instructions are visible and cannot be silently resolved by the client.
A task cannot become complete without an attributable affirmative attestation.
A timed-out or overdue task remains open and visible.
Duplicate completion retries produce one authoritative result.
A completion records instruction version, performer, responsibility, location, result, evidence, and sync state.
A staff substitution preserves the original assignment and substitution reason.
An observation is labeled as observation and cannot be presented as diagnosis.
Emergency escalation shows direct human contact actions and does not claim receipt without evidence.
Delivery, opening, acknowledgment, action, and closure are distinguishable.
A missed task cannot be closed without an authorized reason and terminal treatment.
Shift handoff exposes unresolved urgent work and requires acknowledgment.
A horse move preserves prior and new location, timing, reason, authority, and performer.
The system does not rewrite permanent horse identity or facility hierarchy through care workflows.
Turnout suggestions are advisory and require authorized human approval.
Stale or missing weather data is visibly identified and cannot silently trigger high-risk action.
Protective-equipment instructions include item/type, conditions, inspection, removal, and damage handling.
Owner projections exclude internal staffing notes and other horses.
Material welfare exceptions required by policy cannot be hidden by ordinary visibility configuration.
Required evidence preserves metadata and remains permission-filtered.
Offline screens clearly distinguish synchronized truth from local pending work.
Offline operations are revalidated on sync and receive deterministic final dispositions.
Revoked or expired offline access cannot be used to continue viewing or submitting protected care.
AI-assisted summaries are labeled, reviewed, attributable, and correctable.
AI cannot invoke prohibited care, escalation, diagnosis, compatibility, or completion actions.
Administrative correction preserves original record, reason, authority, and successor linkage.
Care search and reporting enforce the same permissions as primary interfaces.
Operational alerts identify failed emergency delivery, stale instructions, urgent unresolved work, and sync backlog.
Backup and restore preserve care-plan, task, observation, escalation, and evidence relationships.
Rollback does not erase care evidence or create false completion states.
All normative requirements map to acceptance criteria, tests, evidence type, work package, and gate before implementation authorization.
All first-user workflows pass accessibility and mobile-use review in bright outdoor, low-connectivity, and one-handed scenarios.
No first-user enrollment disposition is possible while any relevant P0 or P1 is open or Questions 1 through 5 are not YES_WITH_EVIDENCE.

tests.name: Permission denial for unauthorized care-plan creation
Assignment does not grant instruction-edit authority
Mobile outdoor contrast and target size
Other-horse data exclusion from owner summary
Evidence upload failure preserves task state

golden_paths.name: Morning care round
golden_paths.summary: Manager publishes active plan; staff claims shift; verifies horse; completes water, turnout, stall, and blanket tasks; records one routine observation; handoff shows no unresolved work.

golden_paths.name: Owner-specific blanket change
golden_paths.summary: Authorized owner instruction overrides facility default; conflict is visible; assigned groom changes blanket and attaches required photo.

golden_paths.name: Urgent swelling observation
golden_paths.summary: Groom records visible swelling as observation, selects Urgent, directly contacts manager, delivery and acknowledgment are recorded, and Health domain receives the handoff.

golden_paths.name: Missed night check
golden_paths.summary: Task becomes overdue, remains open, escalates to shift lead, substitute completes it, and the original miss plus substitution remains visible.

golden_paths.name: Temporary stall move
golden_paths.summary: Authorized manager moves horse from turnout to temporary observation stall, records reason and effective time, and later ends assignment without rewriting facility or horse identity.

golden_paths.name: Weather-responsive fly protection
golden_paths.summary: Fresh conditions produce a proposed fly-mask task; manager approves; worker performs and records damaged equipment exception.

golden_paths.name: Offline evening round
golden_paths.summary: Worker views cached assigned work, records completions and observation offline, later syncs; one task accepts and one conflicts because the plan changed, requiring review.

golden_paths.name: Owner care summary
golden_paths.summary: Permitted completion and material exception facts are projected, internal staffing notes are excluded, AI-assisted prose is reviewed, and owner receives the corrected summary.

golden_paths.name: Emergency escalation
golden_paths.summary: Worker selects Emergency, uses direct call action, records attempts, facility plan and horse context are available, and closure preserves professional handoff evidence.

golden_paths.name: Shift handoff after disruption
golden_paths.summary: Outgoing shift transfers unresolved tasks, sync conflicts, location changes, and urgent observations; incoming lead acknowledges and assumes responsibility.

adversarial_scenarios.scenario: Worker attempts to edit medication dosage through care task.
Owner attempts to view another horse through shared location or task.
Staff member marks all work complete without opening individual tasks.
Client clock is changed to make late work appear timely.
Duplicate offline retries create repeated completion or repeated escalation.
A stale care plan is used after authority was revoked.
Free text says the opposite of the active structured instruction.
AI summary converts an observation into a diagnosis.
AI suppresses a concerning observation as low priority.
Weather provider returns stale or wrong-location data.
Two staff members complete the same task concurrently with conflicting results.
Task is assigned to an unqualified worker.
Emergency message is sent but not delivered or acknowledged.
Facility configuration hides a material welfare exception from the owner.
Support agent accesses unrelated care media.
Photo evidence contains another customer or horse.
Device is lost with offline care records cached.
Horse is moved physically but location update fails.
Location is changed digitally without physical move authority.
Turnout template implies a new pairing is safe without human approval.
A worker completes a task for the wrong horse.
A plan changes while a worker is offline.
Evidence upload fails after the physical work is complete.
A deleted account remains visible as anonymous performer rather than preserved attribution.
A task is cancelled to improve completion statistics.
A recurring miss is hidden through repeated supersession.
An owner-facing report becomes an employee performance surveillance tool.
Cross-tenant search leaks horse presence or facility membership.
A service provider receives broad facility access after one visit.
Rollback restores an old plan but leaves new tasks active.
An emergency protective action is taken without later documentation.
A minor or guardian relationship is used to broaden unrelated horse access.
Media retention deletion removes evidence under legal hold.
A system outage causes silent auto-completion or disappearance of overdue work.
Imported spreadsheet rows create active authority-bearing instructions without review.
Owner summary is published from unreviewed AI text.

risks.control: No auto-complete, unresolved queue, escalation, alerts, and audit
Controlled vocabulary, labels, provider boundary, AI prohibition, review
Scoped cache, expiry, server revalidation, conflict and quarantine
Delivery-state separation, direct contact actions, escalation fallback

risks.risk: Owner privacy breach through care summaries
risks.control: Purpose-limited projections, redaction, permission parity, tests
Canonical minimum controls and non-configurable mandatory disclosures

risks.risk: AI overreach into consequential care decisions
risks.control: Use-case registry, deny list, human review, audit, kill switch
Integrity metadata, retention, legal hold, audit, evidence manifest

risks.risk: Metrics create staff surveillance or perverse incentives
risks.control: Contextual metrics, anti-ranking policy, no raw completion-only score

findings.finding: Exact repository paths, versions, and checksums for all controlling and inherited source families are not frozen.
findings.required_action: Source freeze required before implementation authorization.

findings.finding: Cross-PIA contracts for authorization, task scheduling, health, feed, facility location, notifications, media, and offline sync are not approved.
findings.required_action: Approve contract ADRs and versioned interfaces.

findings.finding: The machine-readable companion is documentary and has not undergone schema validation or full forward/backward reference validation.
findings.required_action: Run machine validation and close orphan references.

findings.finding: Numeric SLOs, escalation response targets, retention classes, and evidence thresholds are not approved for production.
findings.required_action: Assign operational owners and approve measurable targets.

findings.finding: No implementation or as-built reconciliation exists.
findings.required_action: Implement only after separate authorization and reconcile before verification.

findings.finding: No executed test, golden-path, adversarial, backup, restore, rollback, support, or incident evidence exists.
findings.required_action: Produce and preserve evidence before readiness claims.

findings.finding: Engineering, QA, operational, and evidence-custodian owners are unassigned.
findings.required_action: Assign accountable owners before implementation or operational readiness.

findings.finding: No controlled first-user cohort, onboarding material, training, support schedule, or release package exists.
findings.required_action: Prepare and approve enrollment package after verification and operations gates.

findings.finding: Facility-configurable terminology may drift across barns.
findings.required_action: Use controlled task and escalation registries with local labels mapped to canonical meanings.

findings.finding: Operational metrics could be misused for simplistic employee scoring.
findings.required_action: Apply anti-surveillance and contextual review controls.

findings.finding: Photo evidence can unintentionally capture unrelated people, horses, documents, or locations.
findings.required_action: Provide capture guidance, redaction, review, and restricted access.

readiness_questions.text: Can engineering build the capability without making unauthorized product decisions?
Can quality assurance determine objectively whether the capability works?
Can a reviewer trace the capability to EquineSync controlling governance and the MIAP?
Can EquineSync safely operate, support, monitor, recover, and maintain the capability?
Can the Founder determine whether the capability is ready for first-user enrollment?

approvals.scope: CARE-FD-001 through CARE-FD-020 approved for documentary drafting
